items.rationale: Promote the easy geometry/household board. I rebuilt the exact fresh dossier against the current full inventory, both selected pending boards and validated rejection tombstones; it matches the supplied binding and has no findings. A1–A4/A7: all 16 tiles are familiar concrete objects with specific, checkable uses, minimum salience 0.80; the geometry instruments have both Romanian curriculum and manufacturer-kit support. No claim depends on generic regional association. B1/B2: all four groups use coherent function or membership predicates and all tiles share the concept node type, avoiding a four-type shortcut. B3/B4: one defensible partition follows ordinary object senses. Floor cleaning excludes a garden rake in ordinary domestic use; the watering can is portable, not a plumbed sanitary fixture; no writing instrument remains to cross-fit a geometry kit. The raw engine fairness count, contested count and type-compatible unfair count are all zero. B5/B6: no strong cross-group edges or mirrors, and the groups contain concrete useful objects rather than abstract filler. B7/B8: floor-cleaning and bathroom quartets anchor the easy board; geometry-kit recognition is the most specific nameable distinction, without an obscure tile or hidden knowledge trick. B9: labels contain no complete displayed member name. A5/A6: no editorial-boundary trigger; maximum full-inventory/tombstone/other-board overlap is one tile, maximum quad overlap one and maximum projected approved member use one. The rejected geometry-plus-writing alternative stays excluded because real kits can contain pencils. This is deliberately straightforward easy classification, not advanced wordplay or a claim of a mathematically exhaustive semantic-partition proof.

Promote the easy circuit/household board. I rebuilt the exact fresh dossier after the Alchimie promotion against the current full inventory, both selected pending boards and validated rejection tombstones; it matches the supplied binding and has no findings. A1–A4/A7: all 16 objects are ordinary named household items, minimum salience 0.85, using recognizable electrical, workshop, seating and cooking functions without regional or adult framing. B1/B2: each member satisfies its group predicate of the same relation type; all four groups contain concept nodes, so differing KG types cannot expose the partition. B3/B4: ordinary manual hammer/screwdriver/pliers/saw senses are tools, not electrical circuit components; a possible powered variant does not change the displayed sense. Seating is designed for sitting; cooking vessels are designed for heating food. No other displayed tile fits these intended predicates equally well. Raw engine unfairness and contested/type-compatible unfair counts are zero. B5/B6: no cross-group strong edges or mirrored pairs, and all groups are concrete rather than abstract filler. B7/B8: seating and cookware are quick anchors; identifying circuit components is the most specific nameable classification, still familiar for easy play. B9: group labels do not repeat tile names. A5/A6: maximum full-inventory/tombstone/other-board overlap and maximum quad overlap are both zero; maximum projected approved member use is one. The earlier writing and bed quads each reused three of four members from tombstoned cx_viata_de_roman_293 and remain excluded. This redesigned board does not remove that novelty debt. Straightforward functional grouping is intentional; no unresolved red herring or obscurity supplies its difficulty.
